_meta: A cluster of nodes electing a leader, used to show that giving every node the SAME election timeout makes them all become candidates at the same instant, split the vote, and elect no one -- repeating forever -- while randomizing each node's timeout breaks the symmetry so one node times out first, gathers a majority, and wins in a single round. In a leader-election protocol, when the current leader fails each follower waits an election timeout and then starts an election: it increments the term, votes for itself, and requests votes from the others, and a candidate becomes leader only if it collects a majority. The failure is symmetry. If every node uses an identical fixed timeout, they all time out together, all become candidates in the same term, and all vote for themselves, so each candidate has exactly one vote and none reaches a majority -- a split vote, no leader elected. The term ends, everyone times out together again, and the election repeats indefinitely with no progress. The fix is to randomize the timeout per node so the values differ: the node with the smallest timeout becomes a candidate first, and because the others have not timed out yet they grant it their votes, so it reaches a majority and is elected before anyone else starts. This models a follower granting its vote to the first candidate that asks, and the earliest-timing-out node asking first. On this fixture five nodes need a majority of three: with equal timeouts every candidate gets one vote and no leader is elected, while with distinct timeouts the earliest node collects all five and wins. The node count and the two timeout assignments are the fixture; each election's votes, majority, and winner are computed. Stdlib only.
